At Girls on the Run Philadelphia, teaching essential life skills is the cornerstone of our research-based programs. Trained volunteer coaches facilitate lessons that blend physical activity with life skill development, including managing emotions, fostering friendships, and expressing empathy.

Girls on the Run inspires individuals of all abilities to discover, build, and grow their self-confidence. Together, they experience a sense of belonging and connection as a team. Volunteer coaches facilitate lessons that blend physical activity with life skill development, including managing emotions, fostering friendships, and expressing empathy. At the end of the season, the team completes a Community Impact Project and a 5K together, which provides a tangible sense of accomplishment and sets a confident mindset into motion.

Heart & Sole is an after-school program specially designed to meet the unique needs of girls in grades 6 to 8. Led by trained, caring coaches, the program creates a welcoming space where girls can explore the experiences that come with middle school, build meaningful connections, discover their strengths, and celebrate what makes them unique. Through relevant activities, real conversations, and inclusive physical activity, girls strengthen practical skills they can use in their everyday lives. At the end of the season, participants come together to complete a 5K Celebration.

The Girls on the Run researched-based curriculum is structured around understanding ourselves, valuing relationships and teamwork, and recognizing how we can shape the world at large. Participants gain critical life skills that strengthen their potential at a time when societal pressures and conflicting messages about how to feel and act can cause doubt and uncertainty.

Lessons are designed to build self-worth and help participants feel greater confidence in who they are. Activities help participants recognize their personal strengths and teach them how to stand up for themselves and others.

Our program provides skill-building experiences to nurture physical, social and emotional competencies that can be applied in other areas of life such as home, school and in the community. Completing a 5K at the end of the season gives participants a tangible opportunity to apply what they learned.

Throughout each season, participants learn to respond to others and themselves with care and compassion. Lessons and activities further develop their abilities to sympathize and empathize both within and beyond their social groups.

Girls on the Run lessons focus on cooperative skills and team building through a positive group setting. Participants learn firsthand how to create positive connections with parents and caregivers, teachers, peers and their communities.
By gaining awareness of the power they possess to make intentional decisions, participants learn to choose positive actions which demonstrate respect and responsibility towards themselves and others.

When participants develop and strengthen these life skills, they can thrive. More importantly, they can then develop a final skill: CONTRIBUTION. Girls on the Run inspires participants to build lives of purpose and to make a meaningful contribution to community and society. This comes to life through a key element of the curricula when each team creates and executes a community service project.
We believe that every girl is born with limitless potential.

Our Out of School Time (OST) is designed to meet the needs of working families of youth in grades K-12. All program sites are staffed with highly qualified and trained program staff and are licensed through the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, Division of Child Development. Programing is designed to complement rather than duplicate the school day by giving youth the opportunity to explore and build on individual interests and skills. Students can relax and unwind, join a special interest club, play sports and games, and socialize with peers and adults.
Our OST After School Programming goals are as follows:
• To assist youth in meeting state standards for core academic subjects by providing students with academic enrichment opportunities after school and during summer recess.

• To offer youth participants a broad array of other services and programs, such as art, music, recreation activities, character education, career and technical training, drug and violence prevention programming, and technology education.
• To provide educational services for families of participating students, such as literacy instruction, computer training and/or cultural enrichment.
• To mobilize school, community, and private sector social and health services support and resources in order to remove barriers that impede students’ learning.

Our OST Before Care Programming is a free program designed to bridge the gap between the time parents need to leave for work and the time school begins, offering a structured and safe environment for youth and children in grades kindergarten through the eighth grades.
Key Features and Benefits of the Before Care Program:
• Safe and supervised environment: Our before care programs offer a secure space where breakfast is provided for program youth while their parents are at work.
• Structured activities: Our program provides a range of activities, including games, creative arts, and even homework assistance, to engage the youth before the school day begins.
• Convenience for parents and working families: Our before care program help working parents by providing a reliable solution for childcare before school hours.
• Social and emotional development: Program staff provide enrichment and learning activities that support and promote social and emotional skills development.

To register: Families can pick up paper applications at the school or program sites. The link to the online applications are provided via flyers, class dojo, and in the school district program locator.

Once we receive the applications, a designated staff member will contact the parent/guardian to discuss next steps. Families are typically contacted within one week of application submission. If we have all of the required enrollment information and documents, a confirmation letter will be emailed to the families to confirm enrollment.

Our OST programs do not discriminate on the basis of sex, race, color, national origin, and ethnic background. Youth of all backgrounds and abilities are encouraged to enroll. Enrollment is open to youth with special needs and/or disabilities where reasonable accommodation program modifications are required. The youth must be self-sufficient and able to function in a group setting. Parents should notify program supervisors of any known medical conditions prior to enrollment.

GPCA Summer Camp Programs provide breakfast, lunch, and snacks, in addition to academic and extracurricular activities to support the retention of students’ in-school knowledge while emphasizing team building among their peers. Our students attend weekly trips that are educational, and full of adventure. Swimming, sports, dance, karate, golf, arts and crafts are also an integral part of the curriculum and daily activities.

The Nebinger PTA is dedicated to enhancing the academic experience of Nebinger students by supporting a range of programs, with a focus on clubs in the arts and sciences. Through funding and volunteer engagement, we strive to cultivate initiatives that enrich student learning, while ensuring that our established programs continue to evolve and meet the dynamic needs of our school community.

Our fantastic art teacher, Mrs. Grace, runs the Drama Club with support from drama teaching artists. Each year, the students perform original takes on well-loved stories, like a Punk Rock Peter Pan, a body-positive Little Mermaid, and a twist on Aladdin with the city as the backdrop. The PTA is proud to fund the cost of hiring the teaching artists who help our students shine line the stars they are!

The PTA has committed a significant portion of our budget specifically for transportation for field trips. We feel that students in all grades should have access to the enriching trips our teachers organize! These funds ensure that students in each grade can take one free field trip during the school year.

Each school year, we support school events like the annual Welcome Back Night, Fall Fest, and Back to School Night. We also host Movie Nights throughout the year that are free and open to the community. The PTA is committed to fostering a welcoming environment for all Nebinger families!

The PTA financially supports events like our annual, school-wide Field Day (lovingly referred to as the Nebinger Olympics!), graduation celebrations for Kindergarten and 8th grade, and the Science Olympiad.

The PTA hosts teacher appreciation breakfasts throughout the school year, provides direct funding towards teachers' project ideas with the PTA Classroom Fund, and shows our dedicated faculty extra love during Teacher Appreciation Week. The PTA always looks for ways to give back to those who make Nebinger such an incredible school for our children!
We can't do it without your help!
As a 501(c)(3) non-profit, we rely primarily on donations to help maintain and develop these vital programs. Consider making a tax-deductible donation to Nebinger PTA today.

• Extended school days mean great opportunities for families
Extended school days mean great opportunities for families

On September 3, Mayor Parker’s Extended Day/Extended Year program kicked off in 25 schools across Philadelphia, part of her promise to close the enrichment gap for Philadelphia students and support working families.
The programs are available in 20 Philadelphia School District Schools and five charter schools.

EDEY schools are open from 7:30 am to 6:00 pm, providing free before and after school care. EDEY school will also offer more sports and enrichment programs, including chess, arts, and coding to help students find new interests and passions. These programs advance Mayor Parker’s goal to increase access to economic opportunities.

Students in enrichment programs have better attendance, are often more engaged in school, and feel more like they belong. When children spend more time in school, their grades and test scores improve.
Here’s what you need to know:
• The extended day/extended year programs are completely voluntary.
• While all programs are free families must register for before-school and after-school programs. Registration forms are available at participating schools.
• EDEY programs are run by trusted nonprofit organizations with roots in the school community.
• In the 2024 – 2025 school year, the pilot schools will be open during school district half days, winter break, spring break, and six weeks during the summer.
• Enrollment will stay open until all seats are filled. New enrichment programs will be added throughout the year.

Philadelphia also provides Out-of-School Time (OST) Programs through the Office of Children and Families at more than 100 school sites. Find a program that best suits your child by visiting the city’s OST Program Locator, then reach out directly to the agency listed for enrollment information.

Confidence, focus, and respect, taught one class at a time.
Martial arts for kids ages 4–12, teens, and adults on Jackson Street in South Philly.
on the mat and at home
You may not notice it on the mat first. You'll notice it at home.
• Confidence. The kid who mumbled "hi" to new people starts looking grown-ups in the eye and answering for themselves.
• Focus. After practicing paying attention for a whole class, sitting down for homework gets a little easier.
• Respect. "Yes, sir." "Thank you." Waiting their turn. Small habits learned on the mat that show up at the dinner table.
• Resilience. They miss a kick, hear "try again," and do it. Then they try again on the math problem, too.
• Real skills, taught step by step. Traditional karate and Tang Soo Do, with age-appropriate self-defense and anti-bullying awareness, including when not to fight.
• Every level welcome. First time on the mat, or coming back after years away? No experience or fitness level needed.
Martial arts programs for every age
Fun, structured classes that build listening, focus, respect, balance, and coordination, and are short enough for little attention spans.
When: Mon & Wed 6:30–7:00 PM ·Tue & Thu 4:30–5:00 PM · Sat 10:00–10:30 AM.
Real self-defense, discipline, focus under pressure, anti-bullying awareness, and leadership. Beginner and Advanced classes, so nobody gets thrown in over their head.

Advanced Mon & Wed 5:45–6:30 PM · Tue & Thu 5:00–5:45 PM · Sat 11:15 AM–12:00 PM.
Karate, self-defense, and conditioning for confidence, fitness, and stress relief, at any fitness level, including a lunchtime class on Mondays and Wednesdays.

Made for busy South Philly families
In most South Philly homes with school-age kids, every parent works. We plan around that.
• After-school timing: Kids' classes run Monday through Thursday after school (starting at 4:30 PM on Tuesdays and Thursdays and 5:00 PM on Mondays and Wednesdays), plus Saturday mornings.
• Easy booking: Pick a class online in a few taps, day or night. No phone tag.
• Skip the paperwork: Pre-register online before your first class.

• Simple membership: After your free class, membership is $129/month, month-to-month, with no long-term contract, for 2–3 classes a week. There's a one-time $50 registration fee, and your uniform is free. Family discounts available.
Born and raised in South Philadelphia, Louie Castelli Jr. has been involved in martial arts since the age of 3½, training under his father, a longtime martial arts school owner and instructor.
A 3rd-degree black belt with numerous regional and world championship titles, Louie has spent much of his life training, competing, and helping teach others.

Now, as a father himself, he’s bringing that lifelong passion to his hometown through Philadelphia Martial Arts Academy. His mission is to create a welcoming environment where students of all ages can build confidence, discipline, respect, and leadership skills that last a lifetime.

Before & After School Care Frequently Asked Questions

Step 1: View the programs on this page

Step 2: Access your Y account online
When you are ready to register, login to your Y account online.
• Once you login, click on the Program Registration tab at the top of the page. Choose your Current Location – click on “Change” (or enter school name in “Keyword Search”)
• Choose Child Care from the Categories
• Find the program you need and expand the list of programs for your specific location.
Please note: when you register for child care online, you will be registered for a child care package that includes the entire year of care and any applicable registration fees.
• Click on your desired program option and click Enroll
• A pop-up screen will guide you through the rest of the registration process:

• Select which child on the account you are registering. Helpful tip: you can only register one child at a time. If you plan to register more than one child, we do offer a sibling discount, however, this cannot be applied to online registration. Please call us at (215) 965-4316 to register and receive this discount.

Please note: Each program will show how many children are registered out of the maximum number allowed for the program. If a program is at maximum capacity, you will only be able to add your child to the program waitlist.

• If you are finished all your registrations, click Pay Now. Reminder: If you plan to register more than one child, we do offer a sibling discount, however, this cannot be applied to online registration. Please call (215) 965-4316 to register and receive a discount.
• The Setup Payment tab displays the schedule of payments due at the time of registration and your future payments that will be due.

• Select the stored payment method or add a new payment method. The payment method selected will be used for your payments today and your scheduled payments. You can change the scheduled payment method later by contacting the Y or through your Y account.
• Once your payment is processed, you’ll be offered an option to View or Print a Receipt in the Payment Complete tab.

What are the next steps after I register?

Payment Receipt: Once your registration is processed, you will be sent a receipt to your primary email address on file. You can also access your payments at any time via your online account in the My Account section > Payments and Balances (for receipt details).

Additional Paperwork: Completing your required forms is now easier than ever! You will receive a confirmation email from the Y within a few minutes of your registration that will include a link to My Forms, which is accessible directly in your YMCA online account. You can complete all the required forms and waivers, including immunization records, emergency contact forms, and health history information. This paperwork must be completed before your child’s first day of care and we estimate the paperwork will take about 30 minutes to complete.
After your paperwork is complete a director will reach out to confirm a start date. For more information view our Forms Help Guide
What does a typical day look like?
Your child can expect a day of fun and learning!
• End of Day Small Group Interest Centers
Activities Included: Arts, STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math), Leadership Development, Literacy, Service Learning, Health and Wellness
Who will be working with my child throughout the school year?
Your child will be guided by our trained, caring, and dedicated staff.

At the Y, we believe that our staff is our greatest resource. Our team all have prior experience working with children and have school-age-specific training to ensure they not only provide your child with a fun experience but a safe and educational one as well.

To ensure your child is in safe hands, all staff members must also pass through a rigorous series of background checks including FBI Fingerprinting, National Child Abuse Registry, National & State Sex Offender Registry, and full reference checks.

All staff providing before and after school care receive training on key topics like child abuse recognition and prevention, CPR and first-aid training, character development and group dynamics, and SO much more!
What if I need to change or cancel my registration?
We know that your needs for care may change over the school year. Please submit your request online and a member of our team will follow up within two business days to confirm your request.

Participants sharpen their improvisation skills and ability to perform without a script. Theater games teach characterization, collaboration, and artistic risk-taking with humor and fun. Beginner Jazz focuses on introducing Broadway-style jazz technique, musicality, rhythm, and stretching. Students focus on character-development, choreography, facial expression, body language, and ensemble-based teamwork.

The ballet program focuses on technique and strength training, as well as characterization while dancing. This program is highly recommended for all Musical Theatre students. Combining Cecchetti Method discipline, Graham floorwork and technique, and performance fundamentals, PACK’s modern ballet program builds dancer confidence while preparing an engaging number for the current production. Ballet students are eligible to move up through the levels as they grow as dancers and performers.

Costume design is an introduction to the many skills required to costume a theatrical production. Students will learn to source and repurpose clothing as well as create original costume pieces to suit the current productions. Basic design, sewing skills, and the use of a sewing machine will be taught.

Our youngest students have a blast in this introduction to storytelling through creative movement, ballet technique, singing and dramatic play. A great precursor to production classes, this program allows our smallest PACK-ers to follow directions, work together with peers, and gain confidence as performers. For students 2nd-4th grade interested in production design and costume design. A pre-production technique class to introduce design fundamentals. This class will culminate with an end-of-session art showing.

Junior Company members benefit from a diverse program that emphasizes Broadway-style choreography, group scene work, and singing in character. The performers prepare two musical numbers and a scene for the current show, while learning technique through games and exercises.

PACK LAB is a pre-professional training simulation in which students create and execute their own production under the mentorship of theatre industry professionals. For grades 10-12, PACK LAB prepares young artists for creative careers by equipping them with a full production budget, access to facilities, and professional guidance to help them shape their own project. PACK LAB is an advanced continuation of the skill-building program that begins with early childhood performance education at PACK.

This resume-building program will kick-start career experience, round out a competitive college application, and provide a letter of recommendation for future professional projects or academic applications. PACK LAB students will be encouraged to produce work with a high degree of professionalism, while experimenting and risk-taking in their artistic process. This program is recommended for pre-professional performers, as well as those with special interest in producing, directing, choreographing, designing and/or stage-managing.

Production design is responsible for the overall look and design elements of the PACK productions. Student designers learn to fabricate, repurpose, or source props and set pieces for use in the current show and will learn basic design principles, varied construction and painting techniques, and participate in show-specific projects such as puppet construction. This class requires the use of sharp tools which students are taught to use and handle properly.

Senior Company members dive deeper into learning complex choreography, creating compelling characters, and singing, both solo and as part of a group. The performers prepare at least three musical numbers and challenging scenes for the current production as they practice vocal technique, dance warm-ups, and taking direction.

Certified with the Society of American Fight Directors, Gideon McDonald will lead students in a course about learning safe practices while engaging in stage combat. Students will learn choreography for hand to hand combat, how to fall safely, and single sword technique, and they will also put their character development/acting skills to use as they combine stage combat choreography with theatrical scene work.

A little about Dungeons & Dragons: D&D is a role-playing game (RPG) that was first published in 1974. It is now in its 5th Edition. Players create their own characters to role-play, and groups of characters are called a “party.” The party engages in adventures in fantasy world settings, leveling up and gaining new skills and spells. Party members work together to travel, solve puzzles, battle monsters and foes, and, hopefully, leave their setting better than when they found it. Queen & Rook’s Youth & Teen D&D Programs focus on negotiating as a member of a group, interpersonal communication skills, reading and math skills, fantasy world building, empathy, creativity, collaborative storytelling, and safe risk-taking. D&D campaigns are led by an adult Dungeon Master (DM), who plays all the non-player characters (NPCs) and tells a lot of the story. As DMs in our Youth Program, we choose stories that are child-appropriate and tales that can be solved with negotiation and kindness, in addition to strength.

SOME THINGS TO KEEP IN MIND

Medication (full day/half day camp only): we do not have a nurse on staff. Any student who needs to take medication during the One Day Camp, the parent/guardian must provide any/all medication including over-the-counter medications. All medication must be stored securely (in a Ziplock bag) labeled with the child's first and last name. Student must be able to self-administer.
*In the event of an emergency staff will administer life saving medication: PA Policy
Please complete this medication form and submit to SCP prior to attendance: Parental Consent to Administer Medication

Videos/Photos: we do our best to record shows but we do not have a photographer on staff. Feel free to take pictures and videos of your own. When posting on social media please tag us @sawubonacreativity and #sawubonacreativity.
We will share all pictures/videos with you via Dropbox (you don’t need a Dropbox account to view photos/videos).
Staffing/Volunteers: there will be 2-4 adult staff members in the theatre: 2 teaching artists and 2 teachers aides.

Participation: performance can be a very vulnerable and scary thing. Your child may enjoy learning all about theatre arts, practicing and playing but they may not want to perform in a live show and that is okay. Students who choose not to participate in the live show may have the option of recording their performance to be shared during the show.

Child sensory needs: if your child has any sensory needs please ensure that they have the tools or items they need to be comfortable ie: students with noise sensitivities can bring/wear noise canceling headphones. We take several breaks throughout the day and we take a 1 hour lunch. We have an outdoor back patio where students can get some fresh air.

What Can I Expect From A Full Day Of Camp?
Just like with every program we offer, those participating in a Skate The Foundry Summer Camp can expect an experience tailored to their skill levels and their needs that is full of fun and learning!

We will start our days with a Morning Meeting and a stretch so all of the campers can get to know each other (and us!) while getting warmed up for the day. We will also cover important topics such as etiquette in the skatepark and the skating goals we hope to accomplish both short and long term

From there the day will take off with activities such as group skates (split by age and/or skill level) where campers will have the opportunity to learn new skills from our instructors together as well as less structured free skates where campers can practice what they have been working on as a whole group.
Interspersed throughout workshops, skaters can expect breaks for lunch and snacks to fuel up for more learning and fun (please note that food is not provided, please plan accordingly!).
Summer Camps at Skate The Foundry go beyond skating! Additional experiences potentially include trips to the Art Museum as well as art based workshops to further flex your kid’s creative muscles.
What Do I Need To Bring To A STF Program?
1. Skateboard; penny and longboards are not allowed. If you do not have a board yet or are not sure if your board meets the criteria, please contact us.
3. Safety gear (Knee/elbow pads and wrist guards).
4. Water bottle. Please prepare insulated water bottles for a hot weather.
5. Snack for half day camp. Snack & lunch for full day camp.

Yous Fitfulness (fitness+mindfulness) classes brings kids’ fitness, yoga, and mindfulness to kids ages 1+. Through engaging movement, stillness, and play, kids develop focus, resilience, and a positive relationship with their bodies and minds.

At Yous, every class begins with making fitness fun! Kids engage in developmentally-appropriate games that emphasize teamwork and foundational exercises such as running, jumping, burpees, and planks. Our consistent programming nurtures positive body awareness, fosters a lasting exercise habit, enhances cardiovascular strength, and introduces the concept of perseverance. All of this is done under the guidance of our supportive and knowledgeable instructors.

Following the energetic and heart-stimulating activities, the class transitions into recovery with yoga. Kids love yoga at Yous! Our sessions are engaging and challenging for all ages. Each lesson includes restful restorative postures followed by an active yoga series. Your child will learn about breath control, flexibility , various postures, and techniques for calming the mind.

Finally, kids learn to practice mindfulness, a proven method for bringing calm and focus to their development. Kids naturally take to meditation, which enhances their focus, awareness , and meta-cognition .
Leads every session; 2,000+ classes taught, daily practice of fitness, yoga & meditation.

What are the dates and times of camp?

Even if the camp description on this page says “Sold Out,” we may still have reduced fee slots left. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact the Camp Director at c
Are there benefits for Awbury members?

Members receive 5% off the full camp price and the opportunity to sign up for camp a week before registration opens to the public, so join at the Family Level now to lock in your savings for the summer and to have the opportunity to register early. An email with a link to early registraion will be sent out in late January to all Member Families.
Is there a waitlist for camps at capacity?

If the camp you are registering for is full and you do not qualify for financial aid, your child’s name will automatically be put on a waitlist for that camp. We will contact you as soon as a space becomes available. There is a separate waitlist for campers on financial aid, depending on how many financial aid slots were reserved for that camp. For any questions about waitlists, please email camp@awbury.org
What is the ratio of campers to staff?
For younger campers (ages 5-7), the ratio is 9 campers to every 1 adult staff member; for older campers (ages 8 and up), the ratio is 10 campers to every 1 adult staff member.
What if the weather is bad?

Camp takes place rain or shine! If there is severe weather or a heat advisory, we may bring campers indoors or under shelter for periods of time, or may offer extra water play. If the Air Quality Index (AQI) reaches the red zone, camp will be canceled for the day, as we do not have enough indoor spaces for all campers to be indoors at all times.
What if my child is sick?

If your camper has any of the following symptoms not caused by an allergy: persistent coughing, fever, nausea, rash, sore throat, infection, or extreme fatigue OR has a communicable disease like chickenpox, mumps, or flu OR has tested positive for the COVID-19 virus, we ask that you keep them at home for the day and call us in the morning to let us know they will be absent from camp.

We have After-Camp from 3:30-6pm at the Education Center at the Farm at Awbury. If you sign up before the start of your camp session, the fee $18/day. If you sign up after the start of your camp session or do a drop-in, the fee is $25/day. For campers on financial aid, the cost is $7/day. After-Camp includes a light afternoon snack, free play time, and a few organized activities or games.
What if I need to cancel my camp registration?

If you cancel less than a week after you register, you are entitled to a full refund. If you cancel more than two weeks before the start of camp, you are eligible to receive all but your deposit back ($50 for one-week camps and $100 for two-week camps). Cancellations less than two weeks from the start of a session are not eligible for refunds, unless we can fill your child’s spot with someone from a waitlist. We use camp fees and registrations to hire and train staff to meet our camper-to-staff ratios and to buy supplies for each session, so in many cases the money for your child’s time at camp has already been spent. Thank you for your understanding.

If you are looking for a camp that will spark curiosity and nourish your child’s interest in nature, then look no further! Our camp is a full day outdoor experience meant to inspire wonder and appreciation for the natural world. At Nature Explorers Summer Camp, we engage with our environment and learn about the plants, animals, fungi, and habitats that we encounter. Led by Morris staff and counselors, each day will be filled with games, activities, hikes, science, and crafts.
After you register and pay online, please do not forget to fill out the camp forms ! We must get info about your camper to ensure their safety!

Because our checkout experience also tends to get overwhelmed with web traffic during the opening days, having fewer weeks in your cart improves your chances of success at checkout. If you are interested in registering for more than three weeks, you are welcome to add more camp weeks if available, or join the waitlist, beginning January 30 . Week 1: June 29 – July 2 • Make a Splash

Beat the summer heat by playing in the water! Let’s keep ourselves cool and learn about some different ways that animals stay cool in the heat too. Campers will explore the creek, pond, and plants and animals at Morris in these aquatic habitats. We’ll also play water games, make water inspired art, and spend the hot afternoons cooling off in sprinklers and kiddie pools.

There is so much to see, hear, smell, and touch as we explore the woods and gardens here at Morris. We will immerse our senses in the beauty and complexity of nature and let our creativity run wild. Our daily crafts will involve a variety of media and will incorporate materials that we have gathered from nature.

Have you ever wondered what it is like to be an insect? How do they see? What do they eat? What is it like to have an exoskeleton? Campers will learn about all of this and more when they immerse themselves in the fascinating world of arthropods. Daily crafts, games, and water play will also be part of the fun.

Kids are often told not to make a mess at home, but at camp it’s just part of the day. We’ll learn about soil and how plants and animals use this important resource. Plus, nothing beats the fantastically tactile, squishy sensation of mud! Daily exploration and art projects will make use of sand, clay, and mud. We’ll do our best to wash up before going home but be sure to pack extra clothes throughout the week.

Who doesn’t love a cute animal baby? But while some babies are cute and cuddly, others can be slimy or spiny. Some babies look just like their parents, and others go through a process of complete metamorphosis. We’ll look for and investigate different animals and their babies, talk about animal lifecycles, and have all sorts of animal crafts and games.

Let’s show some love to plants — we wouldn’t be here without them! We will see pollination in action, find different seeds, learn about plant parts, and see how plants support all the other living things in the world. From the tiniest seed to the largest tree, campers will explore our plants here at Morris.

Let’s spend the week cooling off in the water! We will explore aquatic habitats at Morris, the water cycle, and do some experiments to learn about scientific properties of water. We will also have daily nature crafts and games. This week wouldn’t be complete without plenty of water play, so every day you can expect us to break out the splash pad, sprinklers, and zero-waste reusable water balloons!

Spend your week being super creative as we reuse, reconstruct, and repurpose a variety of household materials to make “beautiful junk.” We will also be spending lots of time outside in nature, and activities could include making boats to race in the creek, building fairy houses, and finding leaves and flowers on the grounds to incorporate into our art. When not crafting, campers will enjoy outdoor games, hiking, and plenty of afternoon water play to beat the heat.

Are you ready to explore the world of insects and spiders? These small but fascinating creatures live in every habitat on earth, and about 1 million different species are known (with many more yet to be described). During this week, we’ll learn about different species, crazy adaptations, and imagine what it is like to live in the world of arthropods.

During this week of camp, getting dirty will be part of the fun! Much more than dirt and dust, soil is vital to all life on our planet. Learn what soil is made of, how plants use soil, and find critters that call soil their home. We’ll do science and crafts throughout the week using sand, clay, soil, and mud. We might get messy (and wet from water play), so be sure to pack extra clothes.

What do ants, birds, beavers, and spiders all have in common? They are all very impressive builders and engineers! We’ll learn about a variety of animals who dig, weave, and build their homes, and try our skills at doing the same thing.

What makes plants so fantastic? For one thing, they support all other life on this planet through the food chain. We’ll check out some interesting plants here at Morris, discuss plant adaptations, learn some edible or medicinal plants, and learn to ID a few plants to avoid. We’ll have plenty of time to explore, as well as daily crafts and games.
What is a typical day at Nature Explorers Camp?

We emphasize learning about nature, safety, and fun! We spend much of our day outside, and exact schedules will vary by theme and age. Campers always begin their day at 9 am with a morning meeting that includes name games, team building games, and an introduction to our daily lesson. Mornings usually include a hike and nature exploration on our beautiful grounds. Our youngest campers in Little Lightning Bugs also go to Out –on –a Limb (a treetop installation) for a chance to play in the morning before the Morris opens to the public at 10 am. In the afternoon when temperatures climb, we spend some time either indoors or in the shade doing crafts, reading stories, science experiments, games, and water play. While much of our time is outdoors, we do take weather and heat advisories into account and will always prioritize safety.
Can I sign my child up for multiple weeks?

Due to high demand, each child is limited to a maximum of 3 weeks of camp when registration opens in January. We are a small camp, but we strive to offer a nature camp experience to as many children as possible. If you already have 3 weeks, you may add your child to the waitlist for additional weeks beginning January 30.
Am I finished with my registration after I paid on the website?
No. You will receive a confirmation email with your camp forms attached. These must be completed and sent back to us. Download and PRINT your camper forms and return them by June 1 to:
You can also drop off directly at the Meadowbrook Avenue address above for Gates Hall Monday – Friday between 9 am – 5 pm, or at our Gift Shop during business hours including weekends.
Can my child be in the same group as their friend/sibling/cousin etc.?

We only have one group for Little Lightning Bugs (ages 4 – 5), so all kids registered in that age group will be together. We have two groups at the barn for Bloomfield Buddies (ages 6 – 10) and they are divided by age with an older group and a younger group. Groups will be preassigned, and children will be told their groups each Monday. If you have a request for campers to be in the same group, please email the camp director at least TWO WEEKS BEFORE your camp week begins.
My child has a summer birthday — which group should we register for?

We are not very strict about age groupings since this is not an academic program. We can provide guidance and there are some differences in the age groups, but generally the final decisions are left to parents and caregivers since you will know your children the best. Our program is aimed at discovering the natural world and inspiring children’s creativity, and children who are on the cusp will often do OK in either group. Most of the children in Little Lightning Bugs have not started kindergarten yet. Most of the children in Bloomfield Buddies have completed kindergarten through 4th grade. The older children do more walking than Little Lightning Bugs, so be aware of what your child might be capable of. Some kids hate being the youngest kid in the group and love being the oldest, or vice versa. Feel free to discuss if you’re not sure where your child will fit in, but the final decision is yours.
Are there options for before care or after care?
Unfortunately, we do not have the capacity for before or after care. Morning drop-off is 8:45 – 9 am and afternoon pick-up is 3 –3:15 pm.
Are there discounts offered for camp?
We do offer a member discount for all current Morris members at the premier membership levels

. Individual and family level members with youth add-ons will also receive a camp discount. For the discount, the number of campers at the member price must not exceed the number of youth add-ons with your membership. We do not offer a sibling discount.
Is there financial aid offered for camp?
Yes. A limited amount of financial aid is available on a first-come basis to those with demonstrated financial need. Email igrubin@upenn.edu
The camp week that we wanted is full. How do we join the waitlist?

When enrollment is full, you can join the waitlist using the same registration links. Choose your member level or select non-member and hit next. You'll see a message in red that reads "0 tickets available"; scroll down and click the button "add to waitlist." If you are not yet logged in, you will be prompted to login or create a new account. Then type in the number of children (participants) you wish to add to the waitlist for that date/age group. Hit "add to waitlist" again. Your confirmation will show in the box. There’s a lot of clicking, but make sure you can see your waitlist request in the box at the end. There is no charge to be waitlisted, and spots do become available between now and summer.
How do I find out if I correctly registered for the right camp week, or if I am on the correct waitlist?

Please look closely at your confirmation emails to verify camp dates, age groups, and waitlist requests (the emails will also include the camp forms that you need to complete). You can also view all your reservations in one place via your Morris account. From the main website, login to your Morris account

(login button is on the top right). After entering your username and password, click “account” on the right-hand side, and from the drop-down menu select “My Reservations.” Here you can view all current reservations, past reservations, and waitlist entries.
Planning ahead can be challenging for everyone, but please be mindful when making your camp registrations. We often cannot accommodate requests to change scheduled weeks since we fill up quickly.
• Cancellations up to May 20 : A $50 fee will be deducted from a refund for each week canceled.

• After May 20 : Refunds will ONLY be issued for extenuating circumstances and are at the discretion of the Camp Director. If a replacement is found from the waitlist, a refund may be granted minus a $75 cancellation fee.

Camp is held rain or shine. Campers may still be outdoors in light rain, so please dress your child in clothing that can get wet or dirty and send extra clothes and/or rain gear! In the case of lightning, activities will be moved indoors. During a heat advisory, strenuous activity will be avoided. In addition to morning creek walks about once a week, we will do water play (sprinklers, wading pools, water games, etc.) in the afternoons to help cool off. In an extreme heat advisory, we do have air-conditioned spaces for campers to use in the afternoon.

While a rainstorm will not deter us from camp activities, the Morris Arboretum & Gardens does reserve the right to cancel or shorten a camp day if the conditions are unsuitable and/or dangerous due to extreme weather or air quality. While it is very unlikely that we will ever cancel, if more than half of a camp week is cancelled due to weather, then a half tuition refund will be issued to all registrants. If less than half of a camp week is cancelled, then no refund will be issued.
Is a nature camp right for my child?

It is our hope to inspire a love of the outdoors in all participants. We spend most of our day outside in nature — not in air conditioning. Campers must be able to hike and navigate uneven terrains throughout Morris Arboretum & Gardens. Together we enjoy fun activities under careful supervision of camp education staff. With the guidance of educators, campers must listen to directions, stay with the group, adhere to camp rules, and take accountability for their own safety. Please see Parent Handbook
for more information about our camp and rules.
My child has special needs. What sort of accommodations are available?

Our primary goal is providing a safe, fun, and positive camp experience for children. We can accommodate a wide variety of needs; however, we do hike every day, and our camp staff is unable to provide one-on-one supervision without neglecting their responsibilities for the rest of the group. We are often outdoors, in a less-structured environment than at school. If your child receives assistance at school, we highly recommend sending an aide, TSS, or care facilitator to camp as well. This might be part of a child’s IEP and can be discussed with your school. If your child will have an aide or therapist coming to camp, please notify our Camp Director Ilana Grubin at igrubin@upenn.edu
What should we bring to camp? Do you provide food or lunch?

Campers should bring a backpack with the following items: lunch, snacks that can be carried on a hike, refillable water bottle, change of clothes, and water shoes. Water shoes will stay at camp throughout the week and come home on Friday. Please label all items. Less is more! Please do not bring toys, phones, cameras, electronic devices, money, or valuables to camp. The fewer items that your child brings the better!

Please dress your child in clothes that can get dirty! Make sure your child’s shoes are comfortable to walk in since we will be spending a lot of time on our feet. Flip flops and open-toed shoes are NOT permitted for running games and hiking. Some sturdy open-toe sandals are OK as water shoes, but these cannot be worn all day. Hats, comfortable clothing, and sneakers are strongly encouraged.
We do not provide lunch, so each child needs to bring lunch and snacks from home. We don’t like see
Can I stay at the Morris after I drop my child off?

Unfortunately, families cannot stay on the grounds after a child is dropped off: However, they are welcome to walk the Morris public gardens once we officially open at 10am. You may also stay for a visit after pickup at 3 pm.
What happens if I am late dropping off or picking up my child?

Drop off begins at 8:45 am each day. We usually begin morning meetings at 9 am, and by 9:30 am our campers could be off exploring the gardens. Please let us know ahead of time if there will be a late drop off or early pickup since our campers have over 100 acres to explore, and it can be very tricky for counselors to make separate arrangements. The camp director will help figure out the best timing and location to find the group (usually snack or lunchtime). If a camper will be late due to unforeseen circumstances, please call 215.247.5777

x125 and leave a message. Afternoon pickup is from 3 – 3:15 pm. There is a grace period of one late pickup, but after the first infraction campers picked up after 3:15 pm will be charged a late fee of $5 for every 5 minutes late.
Do you have any opportunities for young teens to participate in camp?

Yes! We have a Counselor in Training (CIT) program for young teens ages 12 –15. The CIT program is designed to provide teens with leadership development and work-readiness skills as they discover personal interests and preferences. Participants will grow as individuals and leaders, gain confidence, learn about caring for children, and HAVE FUN at camp. This is an unpaid, three-week experience, where teens will receive daily training from Morris staff. Because of restrictions on staff funding to run the CIT program successfully, priority will be given to Philadelphia public school students. We also love to hear from our former campers who want to come back, and everyone is welcome to apply. Please fill out this interest form
and we will get back to everyone in January with zoom links for the information sessions and the application form.
Who can I contact if I have any other questions?
Please email additional questions to our camp director Ilana Grubin at igrubin@upenn.edu

Summer is more fun on the water at Seaport Summer Camp, which is back in session for another season! Campers will explore the history of the Philadelphia region through the lens of the Delaware River with days full of hands-on crafts and activities, on water exploration, visits to the museum’s history ships, and more. If your child is between the ages of 6-11, this is the camp for them. Come join us!
Camp runs Monday – Friday, 8 AM – 3 PM. Aftercare is available from 3 – 5:30 PM.

Steam powered many vessels along the Delaware River; it even powered Olympia! So, let STEAM power your camper’s imagination and have them spend a week learning the science, technology, engineering, and math behind this force. Plus, through art and history, we will explore how steam shaped our world.
Aftercare is an additional $150.00/camper per week. Aftercare runs from 3 PM to 5:30 PM, Monday through Friday of camp.
Last day to sign up is June 17, 2026.
July 6 – 10: Revolution on the Waterfront - Celebrating 250 Years of the Delaware River

Can’t let the 250th birthday of the United States sail by us! Spend a whole week dedicated specifically to Philadelphia and our nation’s big summer. Campers will explore centuries of U.S. history through the lens of the Delaware River and also dabble in some sports, too (perhaps there will be a future Olympian amongst us!).
Last day to sign up is June 30, 2026.

Get lost in the fun of early navigation! How did sailors find their way on the early seas without GPS? From sextants to stars, campers will learn all about navigation through hands-on activities and interaction with the museum’s collections.
Last day to sign up is July 7, 2025.

Being moored in front of Olympia , sometimes people forget that Becuna exists! This week of Seaport Summer Camp turns that notion completely on its head. Campers will learn all about “Becky” and other underwater adventures. Get ready to dive deep with special tours, crafts, and more!
Last day to sign up is July 14, 2025.

Typically, Seaport Summer Camp features only three days with time out on the water. This week, campers get on-water time all five days of the week! Spend more in-depth time with the row boats and kayaks, while learning all about how we stay above the surface while out on the water.
Last day to sign up is July 21, 2025 .

Not only is the Delaware River home to so many animals, plants, and microorganisms, but it also provides jobs, drinking water, and much of what we Philadelphians rely on! Spend a week of camp learning all about the river’s environment and ecology to be an even better friend of this natural resource.
Last day to sign up is July 28, 2025 .

To celebrate the nations 250th birthday, the museum invites campers to come explore our newest exhibition: Seeking Profit and Power: Philadelphia, China Trade, and the Making of America! From tea to porcelain, campers will get up-close and personal with the stories, objects, and even tastes of the early trade with China through special culinary and food-based lessons throughout the week.

Boni Wolf has been a proud Philadelphia resident for over 30 years and is thrilled to share her passion for food, history, and creativity at the Seaport Summer Camp. With a dynamic background in culinary arts, education, and marketing, she brings energy, warmth, and hands-on fun to every class.Boni currently teaches cooking programs at several Philadelphia schools and organizations and leads interactive pasta-making classes and private events for adults.

At Camp Taller, we believe in the power of creativity to shape young minds. Our carefully crafted curriculum allows students to learn, grow, and thrive in an atmosphere that encourages artistic expression. Beyond the classroom, we take our students on exciting field trips where they can witness arts and culture on a broader scale.This summer is a unique opportunity for your child to explore their artistic voice while gaining a deeper understanding of culture through engaging activities in art, music, science, and more.
As part of our commitment to providing a holistic experience we provide lunch and refreshing snacks throughout the day.
For more information contact Marilyn Rodriguez at mrodriguez@tallerpr.org
Registration opens March 1st, 2026. If you're interested please sign up using the form below!
July 31 | Family Fun Day @10 am - 3 pm
Our rate is $125 a week per child. For financial assistance please contact us directly.
If you qualify for (CCW) Child Care Works formerly known as CCIS, Summer Camp will be free.
The Child Health Report Form (Physical Exam) Form must be completed before submitting the application (Physical Exam can not expired before August)
Proof of income will be required as part of the application process. We recommend having this documentation ready to ensure a smooth transition
Please complete the interest form to receive the application. Once submitted, the application will be sent to you.
Application and paperwork are due by May 31st, 2026. Registration opens on March 1st, 2026
For any questions, contact Jose Ramos at jramos@tallerpr.org

STEAM: Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Math. Engaging with the sciences, technology, math and art through fun hands-on projects. This course aims to empower students to see themselves reflected in STEM and learn in an experiential way that is collaborative and project-centered. Students will learn about plant uses, care and life cycles by nurturing their own garden, along with about Native Plants in Philly, Puerto Rico and Latin America.

ARTS & CULTURE: Kids get the chance to be creative while learning about different cultures, stories, and styles through art. We paint, draw, paper mache and create hands on projects that help students express themselves freely and take pride in who they are and where they come from. I also make sure we highlight the beauty and traditions of Puerto Rico teaching students about Puerto Rican culture through colors, symbols, and cultural art influences that connect history and identity.

CARIBBEAN DANCE & MUSIC: Students will learn about the history and movements of different dance & music styles within the Caribbean to create their own dance & music routine. In these classes students will experience movement as an act of resistance, healing, release and persistence in working toward a finished show to close the Summer Camp.
SPORTS & RECREATION PLAY : Time for outdoor or indoor play to release energy, strengthen friendships, have breaks from structured learning and work up an appetite.
FIELD TRIPS: S tudents are taken on various field trips, past field trips have been to museums like Grounds for Sculpture, the Philadelphia Insectarium and Butterfly Pavilion, and more.
FAMILY FUN DAY: At the end of the Summer Camp, we host a family day encouraging parents and supporters to visit Taller and enjoy a day filled with activities.

The building is wheelchair accessible with 48″ wide ramps and 40″ doorways. Bathrooms stalls are wheelchair accessible. We also have a bathroom with a changing table for parents with infants. We will make efforts to make programs and services available to all our patrons no matter their needs. Please contact us at 215.426.3311 to discuss accommodations.

Join Us For Get the Edge Summer Figure Skating Camp With Special Guest Coach, Olympic Silver Medalist, World Medalist and US National Champion
For Youth Ages 7+ and separate Adult Track for skaters 16+.
Accepting skaters past Basic Skills Level 2 all the way up to

Whether you skate for fun or aspire to improve your skating skills for individual or team competitions, Get the Edge Summer Figure Skating Camp can help you reach your personal skating goals. Our staff of highly qualified coaches are trained in all disciplines of figure skating and are here to help you to improve your skills in a nurturing environment encouraging fun and safety while challenging skaters to take chances and try some new techniques. This camp is designed for youth skaters ages 7 to 15 and Adult skaters ages 16+ who are comfortable on the ice skating forwards and backwards and have passed at the minimum Basic Skills level 2. Our leveled instruction can cater to skaters all the way up to Silver MIF/Bronze Singles.
Youth Skaters: $375/skater ( Sorry but no sibling discounts).
For Adults Only: Partial week rate: $250/skater for any 2 camp days

Camp will include 3 on-ice sessions (approx. 45min each) and 2-3 off-ice sessions (30min each). Our on-ice curriculum will focus on a variety of skills: power, edges, jumps & spins, turns, footwork, dance, choreography, etc. Sample off-ice topics may include stretching, Pilates, yoga and ballet classes.

Our regular camp program will run Monday, August 3-Friday, August 7 from 8:30 to 1:00 daily. Skaters will move from topic to topic throughout the day with their assigned group. Off and on-ice supervision is provided for youth campers. Youth skate tying assistance can be requested although we encourage all skaters to tie their own skates. Sample schedule based on last season follows. Updated 2026 Schedule to be posted later this Spring but expected to be identical.

Skaters will be divided based on a combination of their age and their skating ability. At the onset of the first on-ice session, all skaters will be evaluated and placed into their age/skill-appropriate group. Depending on enrollment, we will strive to have three on-ice levels (Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced) so that all skaters can be both comfortable and challenged according to what they can handle and wish to learn. Skaters will be moved up or back upon request throughout the week as long as the instructors and the skater are comfortable with the level change.

Wissahickon Skating Club was newly renovated in 2019 and has one state of the art ice surface, a very large upstairs lounge for off-ice conditioning, dance and recreational activities, a heated lunchroom and several heated spacious locker rooms and bathroom facilities. All skaters are welcome to use our rental skates for no additional fee for the entire week of the camp.
• A yoga or pilates mat for off-ice stretch and dance
• Sneakers and comfortable clothing for skating and dance or exercise (NO FLIP FLOPS PLEASE!)
• Camper’s own water bottle with name or disposable, and if desired, a snack. A formal lunch and/or snack is not provided.
• Layered clothing, light gloves, thin socks, light jacket.

Open to all horse-loving kids, ages 5-13 who want to learn about horses and how to ride. Daily activities include equine education, fun, and a great foundation in horseback riding and care. Campers learn about safety, teamwork, responsibility, animal husbandry, barn management, and animal behavior. Hours are from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm.
There are eight, one-week camp sessions. Participants may select multiple weeks of camp. Hours are from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm.

Ages 5 to 7 | Camp Fee is $525 | Monday – Friday 9am-4pm.

Polo Camp is for youth who would like to try polo for the first time or for the experienced player who would like to learn more and improve skills. The AM session is for riders that can walk, trot and canter under control. Focus on arena strategy, field positioning, offensive and defensive strategies, penalties, conversion, and riding.

The PM session is for beginner players that can independently tack u p, walk and trot, comfortably under control. Riders learn the basics of polo, hitting, equipment, rules, and safety. Open to riders 8+.

Our summer camps focus on the process of collaborative art making and imaginative play. All campers are taught by professional artists and are accompanied from class to class by travelers (counselors) and junior staff (Shadow Company members).
Imagination camp lays the foundations for effective collaboration as kids play hard with purpose while being introduced to and developing the skills of the creative theater arts.
Theater campers are taught acting, dance/movement, visual arts, and storytelling/playwriting, all of which culminate in their final performance created, produced, and performed by themselves.

SSOT is a four week summer program where students will work with professional artists to bring a Yes! And… musical to life! They will learn the basics of stagecraft, design, rehearsal, and refinement as they build a show designed to be seen by a community audience.

Musical Theatre Creation Camp is a 2-week camp that invites students to participate in the creation of a new Yes! And… musical. They will work on the story, script and music for this new musical to premiere at the end of camp!

Shadow Company is an intentionally diverse community of young people with a goal of building an ensemble of actors who recognize the power of their voice and tell their own stories. In the summer, they participate in a 2-week intensive where they work on artistic skills the lend to the skills needed for a brand new theatre piece for the FringeArts Festival!

Weeklong dance & drama summer camp for ages 5-10: Each camp day includes dance and drama sessions, outdoor lunch breaks, games, art projects and even a trip to a local sprinkler park. On Fridays, the kids show off what they’ve learned throughout the week with an informal 30-minute presentation for family and friends. Every week has a unique theme, so you can sign up for multiple camps and still get a different experience! The instructional sessions are designed for all levels — perfect for kids who are new to the performing arts as well as those coming back to learn more.

At ZoomDance Camp there’s plenty of opportunity for all kids to expend energy, express themselves, make friends and find something new they love.

Mornings are spent exploring a variety of different movement classes, group activities, art projects and dancing. Each day will feature ZoomDance curriculum and games centered around our favorite stories within the weekly theme. There will also be themed invitations for the kids to create and engage during freeplay times, including dress up, fort-building, tactile bins, calm zones, art projects and pretending.

Afternoons we have picnic-style lunch, quiet rest and reading time, or nap opportunity for those who need it, playground or park trips, and weekly water play. We’ll finish the day with big group movement games, an obstacle course, or community circle time.

Our low teacher-to-child ratio means plenty of personalized attention and a great environment for young children and even for a first camp or drop-off experience. Parents receive photos and activity updates regularly.

Our location at 9th & Reed in South Philly has great access to outdoor playgrounds and parks. Inside we have two big classrooms, a treehouse fort room, and a kitchen giving us plenty of space to dance and play and create.
During some activities, kids are separated by age range for specialized instruction. Other times we have mixed age groups, allowing for expansive play and opportunity to connect and help one another.

Each week at Camp Schuylkill explores a different environmental topic, making each week unique for our campers. Weekly themes are tailored to the developmental needs of each age group.
• During our first week at Camp Schuylkill, we’ll explore and discover how our forest provides food, water, shelter, and space for the many species that call it home.

Our youngest campers will search for signs of animal homes and play habitat-matching games, while our oldest campers investigate ecosystems more deeply—mapping habitats, tracking wildlife clues, and exploring how everything fits together in the forest.
This is a holiday week at camp. There will be no camp on Friday for the observance on Juneteenth.
• We’ll keep our eyes to the skies our second week, as we look and listen for the unique sights and sounds of our local feathered friends.

Younger campers will have fun with bird identification — nest, bird songs, feathers and more — while older campers practice bird watching with binoculars and explore how birds thrive in our forest and city.
12-13 year old campers will enjoy overnight camping at the Schuylkill Center on Thursday this week.
• During Week 3, we’ll make a splash, as we investigate the Earth’s most important resource: water.
Younger campers will learn all about pond dwellers and play water-cycle games, while older campers test water quality and examine how clean water supports all life.
This is a holiday week at camp. There will be no camp on Friday, July 1, for the observance of Independence Day.
• This week, we’ll meet our most important nature neighbors: plants! We’ll learn all about the native plants that live here at summer camp and why they are so important to our pollinator friends!

Our littlest campers will collect leaves, smell herbs, and learn how flowers help our pollinator friends, while older campers practice plant identification, forage for wineberries, and investigate how plants shape our ecosystem.
• During week 5, we get down and dirty!

Younger campers will flip over rocks, peek into logs, and dig in the dirt search for our creepy crawly friends, while older campers examine insect habitats, learn about decomposers, and take a closer look at the tiny creatures that keep our forest alive.
• Urban wildlife plays a important role in our city and in our natural ecosystems. Campers will learn how Philly’s animals, raccoons, opossums, foxes, pigeons and more, adapt to life in the city.
Younger campers will be introduced to tracks, scat, and pelts, while our older youth how city animals adapt, track signs of urban wildlife, and investigate how our human habitats overlap with theirs.
• This week, we channel our inner artists!

All ages will get creative as we make our own artistic masterpieces from natural resources. Older campers will have a chance to journey off site to discover other nature-based art forms in our region.
Let’s put our imagination and creativity to the test by looking at the forest in a whole new way!
• Celebrate the end of summer exploring with us! We’ll spend this week having tons of fun before we go back to school.

All ages will engage in our favorite Camp Schuylkill games —scavenger hunts, fort building, relay races, waterplay, and more! We’ll close out the summer with fun, laughter, and forest adventures, crafting memories that will last a lifetime.

• How many campers are within each camp group?
All 4-5 year old camper groups have 18 children per group overseen by 3 educators and 1 counselor in Training. There are 2 groups in this age range: Wiggly Worms and Crawling Caterpillars.
All 6-9 year old camper groups have 16 children per group overseen by 2 educators and 1 counselor in Training. There are 2 groups of 6-7 year olds: Dashing Dragonflies and Amazing Ants.
There are 2 groups of 8-9 year olds: Radical Raccoons and Wild Wolves.
The 10-11 year old camp group has 16 children per group overseen by 3 educators.
The 12-13 year old camp group has 16 children per group overseen by 3 educators.
• My camper and their friend/family member/etc want to be in the same group. What should I do?

All age groups between 4-9 years old are split into smaller groups. To ensure your camper and their buddy are in the same group please communicate with that child’s adult that you are both selecting the same group during the same week(s) when you register.
Example: All Wiggly Worms will be together. All Radical Raccoons will be together.
• Who will be overseeing my child’s camp group?

Camp groups are supervised by adult environmental educators. In addition to our councilors, each age group has one coordinator to assist with group-specific needs. One Councilor in Training volunteer will be paired with each group to assist the educators.

Yes! After camp registration, you will receive a confirmation email with a receipt. Approximately one week before your child’s scheduled camp week, you will receive a Camp Itinerary via email outlining camp activities and general reminders.
• How do I drop off and pick-up for camp?

To drop off your camper, drive down our driveway and into the parking lot next to the Visitor Center. Meet your groups at the designated home base and check in with camp staff. Children will only be released to their guardians and individuals named in the child’s files as approved for pick-up. Families must check in with their child’s counselors when picking up and signing their child out on the daily attendance sheet. Children will not be released to unauthorized persons.
If a family would like to add or remove names from this list, they may do so by contacting Beatrice Kelly at [email protected]

Staff is encouraged to check IDs if someone they do not recognize comes to pick up a child. Therefore, all adults should bring a form of ID to pick up, even if they are on the authorized pick-up list.
• What should my child wear to camp?

All campers should wear comfortable clothing for outdoor nature play. We advise wearing clothes that campers are comfortable getting dirty or wet in. Closed-toed shoes are required. Please no flip-flops or Crocs!
• What should my child bring to camp?
Campers should arrive each day with a backpack containing:
• An extra set of play clothes.
Items should be labelled with your camper’s name. No food will be provided.
• What if my campers’ items get lost?

All items brought to camp should be clearly labeled with the camper’s name. Items left in public areas will be placed in lost and found, located at the front desk in the Visitor Center. Items not collected within two weeks will be discarded. Electronics, cell phones, and toys are not permitted at camp . The Schuylkill Center is not responsible for personal items that are misplaced, stolen, or broken at camp.
• What do you do about the weather?

As a nature center, we have lots of experience with rain, heatwaves, wind, and other weather conditions that can impact summer camp. We have guidelines for our staff based on our experience keeping children safe all through the year. In case of inclement or excessively hot weather, camp pick-up and drop-off will take place inside the Visitor Center, which is air-conditioned during the summer.

Camp continues rain or shine! Campers have the option to gear up and head out for rain play and exploration. If the rain is posing a safety issue, including but not limited to thunderstorms or heavy winds, then we will move each group to their indoor location. The Visitor Center contains a lab, library, auditorium, classrooms and a Discovery Center which our staff used to keep kids engaged while indoors.

During excessively hot weather, we will use the Visitor Center, which is air-conditioned during the summer. Groups will remain indoors when temperature and humidity are very high if our staff determines that it is best for the safety of our campers. Physical activity will be limited during this time.
or more information about how to prepare for the weather during summer camp.
• What if my child is sick?
Please do not bring your child to camp if they are feeling ill. This can include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, new and persistent cough, etc. Please let us know in advance through phone call or email.
• What about poison ivy or ticks?

Our environmental educators are trained to avoid hazards like poison ivy and perform tick checks. We will work with our campers to learn these skills as well. However, be sure to check your child for ticks thoroughly after each day at camp.
• What if I need to cancel?
While we are sorry to miss your child at camp, we understand that sometimes cancellations are sometimes unavoidable.

Summer Art Camp offers weekly artistic adventures and celebrations of creativity, friendship, and fun. Campers enjoy art making of all kinds in a safe, accessible environment with highly skilled instructors.

A variety of thematic camps are designed for different age groups and involve painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, comics, and mixed-media projects in the historic studios of the oldest art school and museum in the United States.
Looking for summer activities for high school students? Check out Summer Academy
our advanced arts program for high schoolers.

Each week of camp has a theme, and you can register for a specific week or for the whole summer, whatever works best for your family. Sessions also include age-appropriate creative play and rest times, reading and storytelling, and socializing. Campers visit museum galleries for tours led by art educators, and occasionally take walks to the nearby park (weather permitting). Every Friday, campers prepare for an Art Exhibition where their work from throughout the week is on view and family and friends of the campers are invited to the exhibition.

Explore the wonders of the solar system, galaxies, and more. Let’s create art that is OUT OF THIS WORLD!
Imagine yourself in prehistoric times and create a colorful world of plants, fossils, and dinosaur friends.
Ready, set, go! Jet set and be prepared to travel around the world to many different locations. Whether we go by bus, plane, or boat, let’s create art about our adventures at every destination.
Gather around the big top for a clowny, zany, and colorful art making experience. Be inspired by the acts, characters, and animals of the circus.

Let’s spend our camp days and hours exploring trees, cool rocks, and flowers! Adventure into the deep blue seas, viney green jungles, and scorching hot deserts. Be a nature explorer and create your own natural habitats of the great outdoors.
Dogs, cats, hamsters, and rats! Do you have a pet you’ll never forget? Or maybe you want one and you don’t have one yet. We will create our own cute little critters, creatures, and pets!

For Juniors (Ages 8-10) and Seniors (Ages 11-14), we have consolidated our classes to the most popular with two sessions of each class: Families can choose which week works best for them, or campers can take both sessions. The first is not a prerequisite for the next and foundational lessons will be given in both.

This elementary level class will cover the basics of traditional comic book drawing. Students will learn the foundational techniques and skills of illustration and narrative art. Projects will surround these through creative and engaging work with classic comic concepts such as character design, line art, and story telling.

An elementary level comic book drawing class that builds on the foundations of classical art techniques. This class can be taken in part with ‘Comics 101’ or by itself. The projects will combine lessons from traditional illustration with imaginative and experimental exercises using multiple materials. Campers who take this class will express creativity through cartoon design, pop art, and world building.

The basics of traditional sculpture at an elementary level class. Students will learn foundational techniques and skills, with new and familiar materials. Projects will include creative and engaging sculpture lessons based on classical art. With materials like cardboard, clay, and textiles. These will include free standing work, wall hangings, and small hand held art, and more.

An elementary level Sculpture class that builds on the foundations of traditional art. This class can be taken in part with ‘Sculpture 101’ or by itself. The projects will combine lessons from classical sculpture with imaginative and experimental exercises using multiple materials. Campers who take this class will express creativity through 3D design, with mixed media, abstraction, and experimental challenges.

The basics of traditional painting at an elementary level class. Students will learn foundational techniques and skills, with new and familiar materials. Projects will include creative and engaging lessons based on classical art such as still life, Landscapes, portraiture, master copies, and more.

An elementary level Painting class that builds on the foundations of traditional art. This class can be taken in part with ‘Painting 101’ or by itself. The projects will combine lessons from classical painting with imaginative and experimental exercises using multiple materials. Campers who take this class will express creativity through themes such as abstraction, color, style, expression, and more.

An elementary level class on the basics of traditional drawing. Students will learn foundational techniques and skills, with new and familiar materials. Projects will include creative and engaging lessons based on classical art such as still life, portraiture, master copies, landscapes, and more.

An elementary level drawing class that builds on the foundations of traditional art. This class can be taken in part with ‘Drawing 101’ or by itself. The projects will combine lessons from classical drawing with imaginative and experimental exercises using multiple materials. Campers who take this class will express creativity through themes such as abstraction, design, expression, and more.

A class focused on fusing the skills of writing and art to create visual storytellers. We will have exercises in the fundamentals of story; characters, story, setting, and themes. The focus of Comics 101 will be on character, with the goal to create a strong character that can be used in a variety of stories (ex. Batman, Spongebob, Adventure Time ).

A class focused on fusing the skills of writing and art to create visual storytellers. We will have exercises in the fundamentals of story; characters, story, setting, and themes. The focus of Comics 102 will be balancing the fundamentals to work on a large single complete story.
A classical sculpture class, focused on building a traditional foundation of skills with exercises such as busts, figures, animals, and more.
An experimental sculpture class, focused on using sculpture as a means to train creativity with exercises in creature creation, toy and plushie design, marionette and stage design, and more .
A classical painting class, focused on building a traditional foundation of skills with exercises such as still-life, portraiture, figuration, landscape, and master copies.
An experimental painting class, focused on using painting as a means to train creativity with exercises in narrative, abstraction, unconventional tools and surfaces, and more.
A classical drawing class, focused on building a traditional foundation of skills with exercises such as still-life, portraiture, figuration, landscape, animal drawing, and master copies.
An experimental drawing class, focused on using drawing as a means to train creativity with exercises in narrative, abstraction, typography, and more.
