Summer Camps and Classes for our Youngest Dancers

Whether you’re looking to introduce your child to the world of classical ballet, build upon lessons and techniques already acquired, or instill in them a love of dance and a true sense of accomplishment, School of Philadelphia Ballet has you covered. Our Summer Children’s Programs aim to instruct, delight, and inspire — all within a creative and nurturing environment led by a dedicated and passionate staff of ballet professionals. Your children will have the time of their lives, make new friends, and perhaps even learn about themselves along the way.

Join us for an enriching experience at our Summer Camps , where your child will embark on a journey of fun, friendship, and artistic expression. Throughout the week, dancers will work together to put on a performance around the week’s theme. Each morning, we will dance, learn choreography, share in snack time, and create performance costumes with materials provided by SPB. With a variety of themed camps to choose from, there’s something for every young dancer to enjoy. On the last day of the program, join us as we showcase what we’ve learned with a special performance for family and friends. Don’t miss this opportunity for your child to let their inner dancer shine!
9:00-10:00 AM – Ballet and Creative Movement Class
10:30-11:00 AM – Craft Time, Materials provided by SPB
Payment is due upon registration. All payments are non-refundable and non-transferable.

Instill your child with a love of dance in our Summer Children’s Program Classes! Our summer classes introduce the students to dance and ballet through movement, music, games, props, and fun. Dancers learn in an organized group setting while exploring the use of their imagination. Each lesson is a positive experience aimed at instilling a sense of self-confidence and self-worth. Students will progress through essential components, including motor skills, spatial awareness, musicality, and body awareness.

Our youngest dancers are introduced to the fundamentals of ballet-based movement through imaginative play, music, and the use of props. This class encourages creativity while supporting the development of gross motor skills, coordination, and spatial awareness in a warm and nurturing environment.

Pre-Ballet builds on foundational motor skills while introducing a stronger focus on musicality and creative expression. Students continue to develop coordination, spatial awareness, and the ability to move as part of a group. Classes foster confidence and collaboration in an imaginative, nurturing environment that supports each child’s growing love for dance.

The Primary level provides a joyful and imaginative introduction to classical ballet. Designed to build fine motor skills and coordination, students explore basic ballet vocabulary while learning key concepts such as balance, body alignment, and spatial awareness. Classes are held in a structured yet creative environment that nurtures each child’s love of movement and music.

Foundations serves as a bridge to our Student Program levels. Students focus on building strength, expanding ballet vocabulary, and developing proper classroom etiquette. Emphasis is also placed on flexibility, body alignment, and readiness for more structured ballet training.

Dancers enrolled in School of Philadelphia Ballet’s Summer Children’s Programs may wear any style of solid color, capped-sleeved leotard that they choose. Please note that dancers in our Children’s Programs do not wear tights. Skirts are not permitted. Year-round students may continue to wear their uniform to class.
Leotards are available in the Philadelphia Ballet Boutique! Shop the boutique at the link below.
• Ballet shoes must have an elastic strap sewn across the top of each foot. Please do not pin or tie the elastic straps, as this is not secure and can hurt your child’s foot.
• The elastic laces on ballet shoes should be tied, trimmed and tucked in the top of the shoe. This prevents the laces from becoming untied during class.
• Please mark clothing, shoes and dance bags with the student’s full name.
• Pink ballet shoes or skin-toned ballet shoes.

• Hair must be pulled back into a neat bun and fastened securely using hair pins and a hair net (found at dance supply or drug stores). There should be no hair hanging around the dancer’s face. Braids must be pinned back so that they do not move. Hair must be done before class begins.
• No skirts, sweaters, or leg warmers.
• Hair should be combed and fastened away from the face if long. Hair must be done before class begins.
Please note that students must wear street attire over their dance clothing when arriving and departing from the studio .
What should I bring to the Summer Dance Camps?

Dancers attending our Summer Dance Camps should bring a light snack each day for snack time. Due to serious food allergies, snacks containing tree nuts or peanuts are not allowed . Dancers may bring a water bottle.
What should I bring to the Summer Children’s Program Classes?
Dancers attending our Summer Children’s Program Classes need their attire and ballet shoes for class. Dancers may bring a water bottle, but it must be left in their dance bag unless needed.
What is the drop-off and pick-up procedure?
School of Philadelphia Ballet’s studios open 30 minutes before first class of the day. Upon arrival, please check in with Reception, who will direct you towards the dancer waiting area.

Students in the Children’s Program may not be left alone without adult supervision. A parent or guardian must be with the student both before the class begins and after class ends. Guardians should be prepared to escort their student and wait with them in the lobby until class begins.

Designed to introduce children to the structure of a dance class, Creative Movement encourages freedom of expression while building a fun and supportive learning environment. This class helps young dancers develop confidence as they participate independently while exploring music, movement, and imagination.

Our Pre-Ballet class bridges the transition between Creative Movement and formal ballet training. Children ages 4-6 have fun and build confidence as they learn simple exercises and combinations that strengthen coordination, introduce turnout, and establish essential ballet vocabulary. While imagination and creativity remain central to the experience, classes begin to take on a more traditional ballet structure, preparing dancers for beginner ballet in a supportive, engaging, and age-appropriate environment.

Young dancers ages 4–6 are invited to step into the enchanting world of The Nutcracker ! Throughout the week, they’ll explore Ballet, Theater Dance, and Pilates as they twirl through the Land of Sweets and bring beloved Nutcracker characters to life. With a balance of structure, creativity, and fun, this camp nurtures imagination and movement.

Ballet 1/1X introduces young dancers to formal ballet training in a structured, nurturing environment. Students focus on developing proper technique with increased attention to detail, alignment, and strength-building. This level establishes essential foundations in classical ballet while supporting growing confidence, discipline, and a love of dance.
Full Day Dance Intensive (6-12 Years Old)

Beginner and intermediate dancers ages 6–12 strengthen their technique and explore new styles in this engaging camp featuring Ballet, Theater Dance, Contemporary, Pilates, and a student-inspired Choreography class. Each day combines skill-building with creativity and fun.
• safe ways to break in the shoes

Serious intermediate dancers ages 10 and up train nearly 30 hours per week in Pilates, Ballet technique (two-hour daily class), Contemporary Dance, Theater Dance, and Choreography. This intensive camp offers an excellent opportunity for young artists to refine their technique, build strength, and deepen their artistry.
Minimum two-week enrollment required. Weeks do not need to be consecutive.
Appropriate for dancers who have completed one year of Ballet 3, 3X, 4, or 4X at PDA, or for dancers with at least four years of ballet experience.

For intermediate and advanced dancers ready to take their training to the next level, this five-week intensive offers an immersive and inspiring experience. Dancers refine and elevate their ballet technique while expanding their versatility and artistic expression through classes with Philadelphia Dance Academy faculty and esteemed guest artists.
Designed for current PDA students in Ballet 5/5X or 6/6X/7, and for dancers ages 13+ with five or more years of ballet training. Pointe work is required.
Ballet Technique, Pointe, Contemporary, Modern, Theater Dance, Hip Hop, Pilates, Yoga, Franklin Method, Conditioning/Injury Prevention, Choreography Composition, and Ballet Terminology.

Kindergarten to 8th Grade. Kids in this class will be on the move! Obstacle courses, games, jumping, running and balancing are just some of the physical challenges students will be exposed to in this class. Teamwork and cooperation are encouraged, as well as developing physical confidence.

What does my preschool gymnast(s) do in class? Phillyinmovement
What does my preschool gymnast(s) do in class?
• Begin with a fun warm-up utilizing basic exercises and body positions
• Multiple classes warm up together and then separate into groups
• Child’s age is the determining factor for class placement
• Depending on the size of the class, groups may change periodically. Regardless of grouping, students work on skills appropriate for their class
• All classes follow a curriculum that creates a fun environment where we build a strong foundation for gymnastics
• Gymnasts learn skills on the vault, bars, balance beam, floor and trampoline
What does my school aged gymnast(s) do in class? Phillyinmovement
What does my school aged gymnast(s) do in class?
• Begin with a brisk warm-up to raise their core body temperature and to increase strength and flexibility
• Classes are grouped according to age and ability
• Depending on the size of the class, groups may change periodically. Regardless of grouping, students work on skills appropriate for their level
• All classes follow a curriculum and a predetermined rotation schedule
• Gymnasts learn skills on the vault, bars, balance beam and the floor exercise
• Each class has a set list of skills that must be mastered in order to progress to the next level
• At the end of each school aged session, coaches assess students’ abilities using a skill checklist to determine the best fitting class for the next session
• During assessments, coaches will quickly evaluate the set list of skills for each level
How long will my child be in each level? Phillyinmovement
How long will my child be in each level?

• Even though all gymnasts experience the exact same learning, no two gymnasts progress at the same rate. One gymnast may complete a level in one session whereas another gymnast might take much longer. Gymnastics is an individual sport and we believe it is important to encourage each gymnast to focus on themselves and always try their best!
How do I know what level to start my school aged child? Phillyinmovement
How do I know what level to start my school aged child?

• We want what is best for your gymnast. If your gymnast has prior gymnastics experience, please contact us to schedule a free assessment to ensure appropriate class placement. Otherwise, please register your child for Introduction to gymnastics.
